The Experience

Four things that make this stretch of sand different.

Outdoor Training

The Weight Pen sits directly on the sand around a small amphitheater donated by the late Joe Weider — no walls, no membership, just iron and ocean air, exactly as it did decades ago.

The Venice Boardwalk

Skaters, street performers, and the Pacific line the same walk that champions have trained on since the 1930s — Muscle Beach is Venice, and Venice is Muscle Beach.

Bodybuilding Legacy

More than 65 athletes, historians, and photojournalists carry bronze plaques on the Walk of Fame — a living museum you can walk through, free, any day of the week.

The Legacy

Nearly a century on the sand

1934

A group of health and fitness pioneers brings fame to the original Muscle Beach on the sands of Santa Monica, laying the foundation for outdoor bodybuilding in California.

1930s–40s

The scene relocates to the Venice boardwalk, where the Weight Pen becomes the proving ground for American bodybuilding — the original outdoor stage where physique champions are still crowned today.

2000

Joe Wheatley becomes promoter, working with the City of Los Angeles Department of Recreation and Parks and introducing new divisions — Teen, Figure, Bikini, Vintage Swimsuit, Angel Bikini, Men's Physique, Wellness, Classic Physique and Couples.

2003

Don Howorth becomes the first inductee into the Muscle Beach Venice Bodybuilding Hall of Fame, founded by Joe and Christine Wheatley and sponsored by Iron Man Magazine.

2007

The Walk of Fame opens at the Weight Pen on Labor Day, sponsored by Bodybuilding.com and the Deluca family — 23 inductees have their bronze plaques unveiled on the boardwalk that day, including a Lifetime Achievement Award for Jack LaLanne.

2016

The Vintage Swimsuit Class debuts on Memorial Day, a "fit and curvy" division styled after 1940s–50s beach glamour — judged in part by Sara Clark, the original 1948 Miss Muscle Beach.

Today

Three signature shows a year draw competitors from as far as Germany, Nigeria and Brazil, with 65+ Hall of Fame honorees and national media coverage from NBC, Fox, CBS and ABC.
